mcp.name: ai.satoshidata/wallet-intelligence
mcp.description: Bitcoin entity and risk-exposure evidence for AI agents; keyless MCP, no risk_check score/verdict.

reading.body:
Atos holds 88 granted US patents but no tracked AI products, so its patent record is the only hard evidence of what it builds.

The recent patents cluster around configuration management, secure data processing, health records, call handling, and blockchain complexity. None of the five most recent titles describes a compute, power, or data center technology. For a company that markets AI, hybrid cloud, and infrastructure management, the granted claims sit closer to enterprise software and data handling than to the physical layer that constrains AI scaling.

The one AI-adjacent artifact is an MCP server for Bitcoin wallet intelligence, which exposes entity and risk data to agents without returning a score or verdict. That is a tool for agents to consume, not infrastructure they run on. The data does not show how much compute Atos operates, what it consumes, or where its AI workloads are hosted, so no claim can be made about its exposure to the grid constraint.

The profile text is self-reported and includes performance figures, such as quotation processing falling from 24 hours to 2 minutes, that are not independently verified here. The patent count covers grants since 2001 matching the applicant phrase "atos," which may include unrelated filers. Nothing in this data establishes whether Atos owns, leases, or resells the capacity its AI services depend on.

profile_text.body:
Atos is a public company that describes itself as designing digital solutions from the everyday to the mission critical, in artificial intelligence, hybrid cloud, infrastructure management, decarbonization and employee experience. It says it works in mission-critical environments, sovereign cloud, cybersecurity and AI-driven services, and that it aims to bring together human, collective and artificial intelligence to support what it calls a responsible, secure and AI-powered digital future.

On its own account, an initial single AI agent grew into a company-wide AI transformation effort, cutting quotation processing from 24 hours to 2 minutes with 99% accuracy. Atos says that work led to an AI Centre of Excellence that scaled seven solutions and identified 50+ use cases. It also cites work with Defra on end-user services for 30,000 employees, using analytics, automation, refurbished devices and remanufactured laptops.

The company's record includes no tracked products and no lawsuits. It is associated with an MCP server named ai.satoshidata/wallet-intelligence, described as providing Bitcoin entity and risk-exposure evidence for AI agents; the server is keyless and does not return a risk_check score or verdict.
